risk_flags.reason: Red-path edit to middleware.js (auth-critical). This is the exact change pre-approved under DEC-N21/P1C: adds isNotesRoute matcher + hasNotesAccess gate block layered after the existing auth.protect(), with no change to isPublicRoute or auth.protect() behavior. Scanner's two P1A auth_clerk hits (scanner_report.json:7-23) are this enumerated pre-approved item, so route is logged_only, not an escalation.

failure_classification.evidence: No prior failures recorded for this chunk and no failures this turn; executor_report.json reports an empty failures array and the manual matrix shows 9/9 pass.

evidence.claim: Gate is layered AFTER the existing auth.protect() call and only on /notes and /api/notes, leaving isPublicRoute and auth.protect() untouched — satisfies criteria 1, 2, 5 and stays inside DEC-N21 exact scope.

Flag check reads sessionClaims.publicMetadata first and falls back to currentUser() only when publicMetadata is absent from the session token (=== undefined), matching criterion 3; default is fail-closed (hasAccess only true on explicit === true).
Unauthorized /api/notes requests get 403 JSON via pathname.startsWith('/api/notes'); all other unauthorized notes requests redirect to / — satisfies criterion 4.
Only middleware.js changed; no schema, route-config, or data-access changes — config matcher block is unchanged in the diff.
Manual route matrix evidenced: 9/9 pass across two accounts, including controls 7-9 confirming auth.protect() and public-route behavior unchanged, and case 5 confirming API 403 JSON without redirect.
The middleware edit is pre-approved as a specific enumerated item (DEC-N21, human) with exact_scope matching the implemented change; work stays inside those bounds.
